newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen easier on hopes for official remarks.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen easier on hopes for official remarks.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures were easier in late morning on Friday.
Bearishness was attributed to expectations that a senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara may urge higher Japanese interest rates in an interview.
Sakakibara, director-general of MOF's International Finance Bureau, is scheduled to appear on Reuters Financial Television a little after 11 a.m. (0200 GMT).
"The market was sold on expectations that Sakakibara may repeat his recent remarks in which he had called for higher interest rates," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank.
December ended the morning session down 0.01 at 99.06 after moving between 99.05 and 99.09. The contract fell to 99.05 after Sakakibara's comments began at 0223 GMT.

Sakakibara said it is natural for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to raise interest rates when economic strength is confirmed. He also said the possibility of the economy contracting is less than people think and that it is dangerous to assume that Japan will not raise interest rates within a year.
But a trust bank dealer said the market is basically directionless as operators mostly believe that the BOJ will not raise rates for the time being.

"There is still a consensus that the BOJ will not raise interest rates for now. The bank may do so if its June tankan report shows improvement in business sentiment at small- and medium-sized corporations," he said.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate eased to 0.47 percent after the BOJ's more accommodative stance this morning. Thursday's weighted average was 0.51 percent.
"Today's operation was reasonable after the rate's jump to 0.51 on Thursday (from Wednesday's 0.45)," said a bank dealer.
Key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at an unchanged 0.55 percent. --Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
